findings.title: Race condition lets a backup code be reused
findings.body: The backup-code consumption path in authorize() reads user.backupCodes, decrypts it with JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)), nulls the matched slot, re-encrypts, and writes the result back via prisma.user.update with no atomicity guard. Two concurrent requests submitting different valid backup codes both read the same pre-image, each null a different index in their local copy, and whichever update commits last overwrites the other writer's null — restoring the slot the first request consumed. Consequence: a backup code can be used more than once, breaking the one-time-use guarantee the PR explicitly relies on (see the comment 'delete verified backup code and re-encrypt remaining'). Fix by making the update atomic, e.g. wrap read+write in prisma.$transaction, or include the expected pre-image in the WHERE clause so the second writer is rejected.

findings.title: Backup-code login and disable flows are not tested
findings.body: The TODO at the top of the file ('TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup') explicitly states the two main backup-code flows are not covered. The added e2e block only exercises the download/copy buttons in the setup screen and never actually submits a backup code during login or disable. The PR description also says 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works'. Without these tests, regressions in code matching, case normalization, the one-time-use guarantee, and the race condition in next-auth-options.ts would not be caught. The two inline TODOs ('check file content', 'check clipboard content') further leave the new UI assertions unchecked.

findings.title: Disable endpoint logs a 'backup code login' error
findings.body: The console.error inside the backup-code branch logs 'Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login.' This handler lives at /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable, not a login endpoint. Operators reading server logs during a disable incident will be misled into believing a login attempt failed. The same wording is reused in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:133, suggesting copy-paste rather than intent. Update the message to reflect the actual operation (e.g. 'cannot proceed with backup code verification while disabling 2FA').

findings.title: Backup-codes Blob URL is never revoked when the modal closes
findings.body: handleSetup calls URL.createObjectURL(textBlob) to produce the download link for the user's plaintext backup codes and stores it in backupCodesUrl. There is no URL.revokeObjectURL call when the modal closes — resetState() only clears password, errorMessage, and step, and the component has no unmount cleanup. The Blob keeps the user's plaintext backup codes alive in memory until either the next successful setup (which revokes the previous URL) or the page is unloaded. Revoke the URL inside resetState and in a useEffect cleanup that runs on unmount.

findings.title: Default export is named TwoFactor instead of BackupCode
findings.body: The new file apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx declares 'export default function TwoFactor(...)', yet consumers import it as 'import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"' (see DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8 and login.tsx:32). The symbol name in the file does not match the imported name. A developer greping for TwoFactor (e.g. while refactoring or deleting the existing apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx) will edit the wrong file, and tools that flag mismatched export/import names may warn. Rename the export to BackupCode to match the file name and the import sites.
